note: The Apr. 24, 1908 order on this page amends Canal Zone law on defacing boundary monuments, not the San Juan National Forest order.
The Aug. 14, 1908 order on this page amends Canal Zone Penal Code section 344 on grand larceny, not the Bataan and Cacraray military reservations.
The only Oct. 21, 1908 order on this page amends the unskilled-laborer regulations in Washington, not Schedule A Treasury positions.

signature_on_page: Theodore Roosevelt. The White House, October 21, 1908.
first_words: The regulations governing the employment of unskilled laborers at
last_words: regulations except as provided in Regulation XI hereof.
note: Order of Oct. 21, 1908 adding Regulation XI to the unskilled-laborer regulations begins under a dated heading on this page and runs onto the next page, which has the Roosevelt signature and White House dateline.
There is no order about Frederick Koch or the Carlisle Indian School here; the Oct. 21, 1908 order on the page concerns unskilled laborers.
The Dec. 23, 1908 items on this page are the gold-employee order and the Gudger and Owen court appointments, not the Cuba provisional-administration transfer order.

signature_on_page: Wm. H. Taft. The White House, March 23, 1909.
first_words: Civil Service Rule X, paragraph 8, clause (e),
last_words: the manner provided by the Civil Service Art
note: Full text of the order amending Civil Service Rule X, paragraph 8(e), on proposed transfers, signed Wm. H. Taft, The White House, March 23, 1909 (the OCR reads 'Art' for 'Act').
The June 25, 1909 order on this page fixes Saturday hours (cited as EO 1096), not Arthur F. Statter's Treasury appointment.
The July 30, 1909 orders on this page cover good-behavior credit for convicts and the penalty for murder, not Grand Army of the Republic leave.
The only Feb. 8, 1910 reference is a footnote to an order on oaths for the Board of Local Inspectors, not the Schedule A War Department order.
